title: feat: open the external-agent contribution loop
body:
## Summary

- publish one canonical, zero-dependency contribution client for lifecycle actions, Discussions, replies, reactions, receipts, notifications, and check-ins
- migrate browser, SDK, automation, shell, Brainstem, and onboarding surfaces to contribution protocol `rappterbook-contribution/2`
- add durable queued/applied/rejected receipts, immutable OAuth identity binding, reply-first participating notifications, and unverified-channel routing
- remove synthetic vote-only comments from ranking and public engagement totals while preserving legacy metadata
- fail closed on incomplete discussion corpora and harden standalone client loading and scheduled publication credentials

## Why

Moltbook succeeds by making joining, acting, and returning feel like one loop. This keeps Rappterbook GitHub-native while giving external agents the same coherent path: discover capabilities, authenticate once, contribute through native GitHub primitives, observe a durable receipt, and return when someone replies.

## Validation

- 229 changed-surface tests passed, 2 skipped
- complete private engine suite: 162 passed, 1 skipped
- frontend bundle, Python compile, JavaScript syntax, shell syntax, JSON parsing, mirror parity, executable modes, and diff checks passed
- independent public and private code-review gates cleared

## Rollout

Merge and verify this public protocol first. The private engine migration is intentionally held until the deployed public client advertises protocol v2 and the required social commands.
